title: Vesper and the Summer
premise: Dominic Montrose fled his coastal hometown after a betrayal that ended his engagement, burying himself in turtle conservation on a distant island. When his estranged father dies and wills the family orchard jointly to Dominic and Vesper, the childhood friend who was the other half of that betrayal, Dominic returns intending to sell his half and vanish. Forced to spend a summer restoring the dying orchard together, he uncovers the truth about what Vesper actually did and why his father bound them to the land, and must finally confront the man he became to survive his grief. In the end, Dominic chooses to keep the orchard, forgive Vesper, and forgive himself, letting the first harvest in a decade ripen as love stops being past tense.
about_author: Dominic Montrose is the pen name of a former field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters after a decade studying sea turtle nesting sites across the Pacific. He writes romance about people who mistake distance for safety, from a cottage that smells permanently of salt and citrus.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On his research island, Dominic narrates his ordered, armored life—nightly nest counts, no attachments, love kept firmly past tense. A lawyer's letter arrives: his father is dead, and the orchard deed names two owners. Emotional beat: the first crack in his invisibility; he books a ferry he swears is temporary.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He arrives home to find Vesper already living in the orchard cottage, equally furious and equally bound by the will's condition: neither may sell for one summer, or the land goes to a developer. Emotional beat: cold hostility masking old intimacy; they agree to a truce of silence and separate sides of the orchard.

chapters.title: The Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper tends the neglected trees alone, revealing through memory that he grew up half-raised by Dominic's father after his own family fell apart—and that he never stopped writing letters Dominic never answered. Emotional beat: longing under resentment; the reader learns Vesper's side of the estrangement is not what Dominic assumes.

chapters.title: Blight
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A fungal blight threatens the orchard, and the county inspector warns that a dead orchard voids the will's protection. Dominic's marine science proves useless against it; he must ask Vesper, who studied horticulture, for help. Emotional beat: reluctant dependence; first real conversation in eleven years, all business and trembling underneath.

chapters.title: What Vesper Did
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Working side by side, Vesper finally explains the betrayal as he lived it: he took the blame for a fire that was actually Dominic's father's doing, accepting Dominic's hatred to protect the old man's secret. Emotional beat: confession without absolution; Dominic walks out mid-sentence, unwilling to believe his father could lie.

chapters.title: Letters in the Attic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Searching the attic for the deed's paperwork, Dominic finds a shoebox: his father's unsent letters, Vesper's returned ones, and proof of the fire's true origin. His whole narrative of victimhood collapses. Emotional beat: grief doubled—mourning his father and the decade he lost to a lie.

chapters.title: The Longest Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Midsummer festival in town forces them into public together; old neighbors reveal how Vesper carried the town's judgment alone. That night, storm-damaged trees nearly crush Vesper, and Dominic pulls him clear. Emotional beat: the armor breaks; they admit, soaked and shaking, that they never stopped choosing each other first.

chapters.title: Root Rot
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hope curdles: the inspector returns, the blight has reached the heritage trees, and the developer circles with a cash offer that would free them both. Vesper, terrified of being forgiven out of pity, pushes Dominic away. Emotional beat: lowest point; Dominic nearly signs, choosing flight one last time.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper grafts cuttings from the oldest surviving tree—a technique his late mother taught him—refusing to let the orchard die quietly. Dominic, at the ferry dock with signed papers, sees his own reflection and finally recognizes the man survival made him. Emotional beat: climax of choice; he tears up the sale and runs the road back.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing in Dominic's. The grafted trees hold; the inspector certifies the orchard living, voiding the developer's claim. Dominic and Vesper host the town's first harvest in ten years, his father's letters finally read aloud under the old tree. Emotional beat: resolution—forgiveness given, received, and turned toward the self; love, at last, in present tense.
